title: Cambodian Information Minister: Ceasefire 'Cannot Establish a New' Cambodia-Thailand Border
detail: Information Minister Neth Pheaktra issued a statement rejecting Thailand's interpretation of the December 27, 2025 ceasefire, saying the joint statement 'is not a boundary treaty and cannot be used to alter the internationally recognised border.' He said historical Franco-Siamese maps remain the legal foundation for demarcation, that Thai ground actions -- including barbed wire, bunkers and flag installations -- violate international law, and that the Joint Boundary Commission remains the only legitimate venue for resolving the dispute. 'Military positions may be frozen to stop the shooting,' he said, 'but borders are neither frozen nor redrawn according to where troops happen to stand.'

media.caption: Cambodia's Information Minister says the ceasefire is not a boundary treaty and cannot redraw the border

title: ASEAN Observer Team Inspects Cham Yeam Crossing to Verify Ceasefire Compliance
detail: The Philippines-led ASEAN Observer Team in Cambodia, accompanied by Cambodia's Liaison Group, conducted an observation, verification and reporting visit at the Cham Yeam International Border Checkpoint in Koh Kong province at 9:35 a.m. on September 1. Cambodia's Ministry of National Defence reaffirmed its commitment to the ceasefire and related agreements, saying the AOT's role is 'aimed at promoting transparency, building mutual trust and supporting the implementation of the ceasefire between the two countries.' No violations or incidents were reported during the visit.

media.caption: ASEAN Observer Team and Cambodia's Liaison Group inspect the Cham Yeam border checkpoint

title: Deputy PM Sok Chenda Sophea Tells Belgrade Forum Cambodia Faces 'Grave Challenge' From Thailand
detail: Speaking at a high-level meeting in Belgrade commemorating the 65th anniversary of the first Non-Aligned Movement conference, Deputy Prime Minister Sok Chenda Sophea said 'Cambodia faces a grave challenge to its territorial integrity,' accusing Thailand of unilateral actions inside Cambodian territory -- including the installation of barbed wire, construction of permanent infrastructure, and displacement of Cambodian civilians -- that he called 'faits accomplis designed to alter borders by force.' He said the situation along the border remains fragile despite the December ceasefire and reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to resolving the dispute through dialogue, the ICJ, UN Charter principles and ASEAN mechanisms, alongside the ongoing UN-sponsored maritime conciliation process with Thailand.

media.caption: Deputy PM Sok Chenda Sophea addresses a Non-Aligned Movement anniversary forum in Belgrade
